title: 35:1 desert shall . . . blossom as the rose. Isaiah equates the desert to Israel, an important point to understanding this chapter; here he prophesies that the desert shall blossom, just as earlier he had prophesied that Israel shall blossom (see commentary on 27:6, 10). For Isaiah's prophetic world, the words desert and wilderness relate not only to a barren and desolate land but to a people or nation (1:30) who lack the living waters of Jesus Christ. When Isaiah prophesies that the desert shall blossom as the rose, he refers to the restoration of the gospel: "Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit" (27:6), "Jacob shall flourish in the wilderness" (D&C 49:24), and the full blessings of the temple shall again be made available.
author: Tina M. Peterson
